translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.expectedOutc: After completing the roadmap, learners can recognize common problem types by their prerequisite knowledge and maintain a complete review system spanning linear structures, trees, graphs, search, greedy algorithms, and dynamic programming.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.goal: Complete a systematic training cycle that covers the core data structures and algorithms in a clear dependency order.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[1].fo: Build a foundation in linear structures through array storage, binary-search boundaries, two pointers, and sliding windows.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[2].fo: Practice linked-list insertion, deletion, reversal, intersection, and cycle detection.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[3].fo: Master set membership, frequency maps, and grouping strategies with hash tables.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[4].fo: Practice in-place string operations, KMP, and two-pointer techniques across arrays and linked lists.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[5].fo: Build foundations in stack/queue transformations, expression processing, monotonic structures, and Top K problems.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[6].fo: Systematically practice tree traversal, paths, construction, lowest common ancestors, and binary search tree properties.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[6].ti: Binary Trees and Binary Search Trees
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[7].fo: Use combinations, partitions, subsets, permutations, and board problems to practice decision trees and pruning.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[8].fo: Learn how local choices lead to global optima through sequence, interval, jump, and allocation problems.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[9].fo: Progress from basic states to knapsack, house robber, stock, subsequence, and edit-distance problems.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[10].f: Use monotonic stacks to solve next-greater-element, temperature, rainwater, and histogram-area problems.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.phases[11].f: Cover graph traversal, islands, topological sorting, union-find, shortest paths, and minimum spanning trees.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.summary: Complete a 16-week systematic Chinese practice roadmap covering arrays, linked lists, hashing, trees, backtracking, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, and graphs.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.targetAudien: Learners who want to follow a long-term Chinese knowledge roadmap, know the basics of a programming language, but do not yet have a systematic problem-solving sequence.
translations.carl_algorithm_roadmap_full.title: Coding Thoughts Complete Algorithm Roadmap
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.expected: After completing the plan, learners understand a practical sequence for studying common data structures and algorithms and have a review framework they can continue to extend.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.goal: Build algorithm-practice foundations through a Chinese-friendly learning sequence.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.phases[1: Build foundations in array indexing, two pointers, prefix sums, and matrix traversal.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.phases[2: Practice linked-list rewrites, fast/slow pointers, and deletion boundaries.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.phases[3: Use hash tables for counting, deduplication, set intersections, and two-sum relationships.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.phases[4: Practice string processing, parenthesis matching, and basic stack/queue implementations.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.phases[5: Systematically practice DFS/BFS traversal, tree height, paths, and binary search tree validation.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.phases[6: Practice choosing, undoing choices, pruning, and grid search.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.phases[7: Develop greedy intuition through local choices and interval boundaries.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.phases[8: Progress from one-dimensional states to knapsack and string DP, emphasizing state definitions and transition order.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.phases[9: Complete foundations in grid BFS/DFS, graph construction, and connectivity.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.summary: A 12-week beginner roadmap in Chinese that progresses through arrays, linked lists, hashing, strings, trees, backtracking, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, and graphs.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.targetAu: Beginner to early-intermediate learners who want to build a connected knowledge system through structured practice and prefer a Chinese learning roadmap.
translations.cn_algorithm_foundation_12weeks.title: 12-Week Algorithm Foundations Plan
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.expectedOutcome: After completing the plan, learners can choose a two-pointer, search, tree/graph, or dynamic-programming framework from a problem's characteristics and explain its state, invariants, and critical boundaries.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.goal: Build a stable process for recognizing problem structures, applying algorithm frameworks, and checking boundary conditions.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[1].focus: Start with arrays and linked lists, practicing fast/slow pointers, left/right pointers, and in-place modification.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[1].title: Linear Structures and Two-Pointer Frameworks
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[2].focus: Practice reusable frameworks for sliding windows, binary-search boundaries, prefix sums, and difference arrays.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[2].title: Sliding Windows, Binary Search, and Preprocessing
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[3].focus: Understand recursive and backtracking search through decision trees, state restoration, and shortest-step models.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[3].title: Recursion, Backtracking, and BFS
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[4].focus: Build a tree-problem framework around traversal positions, subtree return values, and binary search tree properties.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[4].title: Binary-Tree Recursive Thinking
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[5].focus: Progress from graph construction to topological sorting, connectivity, shortest paths, and minimum spanning trees.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[5].title: Graphs and Connectivity
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[6].focus: Practice defining states, choices, transitions, and base cases across sequence and state-machine problems.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[6].title: Dynamic Programming State Design
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[7].focus: Practice maintaining state with monotonic stacks, monotonic queues, priority queues, and cache structures.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[7].title: Monotonic Structures, Heaps, and Design
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[8].focus: Use classic composite frameworks to test transfer, boundary control, and data-structure composition skills.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.phases[8].title: High-Frequency Integrated Applications
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.summary: Use eight weeks of focused practice to master core problem-solving frameworks for two pointers, search, trees and graphs, dynamic programming, and monotonic structures.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.targetAudience: Learners who have practiced basic topics but have fragmented knowledge and want to connect problem types through reusable frameworks.
translations.labuladong_algo_thinking.title: labuladong Core Algorithm Framework Plan

translations.leetcode_75_core_sprint.phases[1].title: Arrays, Two Pointers, and Sliding Windows
translations.leetcode_75_core_sprint.phases[2].focus: Build reliable patterns for hash maps, stack/queue state, and linked-list pointer rewrites.
translations.leetcode_75_core_sprint.phases[2].title: Hashing, Stacks, Queues, and Linked Lists

translations.leetcode_75_core_sprint.phases[4].focus: Cover graph search, priority queues, boundary-aware binary search, and basic backtracking.

translations.leetcode_75_core_sprint.phases[5].title: One-Dimensional and Multidimensional Dynamic Programming
translations.leetcode_75_core_sprint.phases[6].focus: Finish the roadmap with tries, intervals, monotonic stacks, and a complete review.

translations.leetcode_75_core_sprint.summary: Complete the official LeetCode 75 roadmap in six weeks, covering 22 core interview topics.

translations.leetcode_top_interview_150.expectedOutco: After completing the plan, learners can systematically solve array, linked-list, tree, graph, dynamic-programming, and design problems and maintain a complete interview review checklist.

translations.leetcode_top_interview_150.phases[5].foc: Practice recursive traversal, level-order traversal, and binary search tree operations.
translations.leetcode_top_interview_150.phases[5].tit: Binary Trees and Binary Search Trees
translations.leetcode_top_interview_150.phases[6].foc: Practice graph construction, connectivity, shortest paths, and tries.

translations.leetcode_top_interview_150.phases[9].foc: Practice bit manipulation, number patterns, geometry, and simulation.

translations.leetcode_top_interview_150.summary: Use the official ten-week LeetCode Top Interview 150 roadmap to cover classic interview data structures and algorithms systematically.
translations.leetcode_top_interview_150.targetAudienc: Interview-focused learners who can sustain a regular practice schedule and want to follow the official Top Interview 150 roadmap.

translations.topic_dynamic_programming_foundation.exp: After completing the plan, learners can explain states, choices, transition order, and initialization by problem type and maintain a taxonomy of common DP mistakes.
translations.topic_dynamic_programming_foundation.goa: Build stable skills for defining dynamic-programming states, deriving transition equations, and explaining solutions during review.
translations.topic_dynamic_programming_foundation.pha: Practice the meaning of dp[i], initialization, and rolling arrays with linear sequences.
Practice choosing state dimensions for grids, knapsack problems, coins, and subsets.
Practice two-dimensional indexes, matching relationships, and string partitioning.
Practice holding/not-holding states, transaction constraints, interval DP, and tree DP extensions.
translations.topic_dynamic_programming_foundation.sum: Use four weeks to focus on dynamic programming, progressing through one-dimensional states, knapsack and paths, subsequences, state machines, intervals, and trees.
translations.topic_dynamic_programming_foundation.tar: Learners who have practiced basic problems but still struggle to define and transition dynamic-programming states reliably.
